subject: Request: Pro-rated SLA Remedy and bridge credit for Nimbus Health outage
messages:
From: Laura Phillips <l.phillips@nimbushealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@nimbushealth.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency + partial outage on 2026-10-31 — request for remediation

Hi Grace,

We experienced repeated latency spikes and short service interruptions the morning of Oct 31 while running our nightly ingestion pipeline. Our ops team captured multiple 5–8 minute windows where responses timed out and several requests returned 500s. This impacted our patient-matching job and delayed notifications to clinicians.

We need:
- A consolidated incident timeline from Redwood for Oct 31 (including region, affected model, and root cause if available)
- Proposed remedial credit or make-whole approach — our procurement lead will expect a pro-rated concession reflecting the impact to our committed throughput for the month

Can you share the remediation approach and an estimated credit the vendor/Redwood can provide? We are trying to finalize our October billing reconciliation this week.

Attachment: uptime_snippets.txt (excerpted logs)

Thanks,
Laura Phillips
Director of Platform Operations
Nimbus Health
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Production latency + partial outage on 2026-10-31 — need exec approval for remedy

Marissa / Karthik,

Forwarding Nimbus Health — they saw repeated latency spikes and a few 5–8 minute outages on 2026-10-31 (US-west region). They asked for an incident timeline and a pro-rated concession for October billing. I've attached the customer logs they provided and our initial uptime report (nimbus_uptime_log_20261031.pdf).

Summary of internal findings so far:
- A lane of queued requests hit a kernel selection path that caused KV cache thrashing under a burst pattern between 07:02–07:18 PT.
- A subset of requests retried, causing client-side duplicate requests and increased tail latency. No broad GPU failure was detected.
- A quick rollback to a compatible kernel variant at 07:20 restored normal behavior.

Customer impact (from their ops notes): delayed downstream ingestion, a handful of timed-out requests affecting clinical notifications. They asked for a pro-rated concession against committed throughput for Oct.

Proposed concession options (initial calc in attached pro-rated-credit-calculation.xlsx):
1) Automated pro-rated credit: 12% credit for October invoice (maps to weighted affected token volume/time window).
2) Short-term goodwill: 1 free month of dedicated throughput at current committed rate + 6% invoice credit.
3) Minimal: one-time $12,500 account credit (does not change invoice line items).

I recommend option 2 for retention — it both offsets their immediate invoicing concern and gives them runway while we validate kernel selection mitigations. Asking for your exec approval or direction to present option(s) to Laura.

Attachments: nimbus_uptime_log_20261031.pdf, pro-rated-credit-calculation.xlsx, customer_comm_draft.txt

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency + partial outage on 2026-10-31 — need exec approval for remedy

Thanks for the write-up, Grace. I reviewed the uptime log and the calc. High level: the incident looks isolated and our rollback was timely, but the customer did see meaningful operational impact and has a committed reserved plan (monthly). We should be careful to balance precedent vs. retention.

Recommended approval to offer Nimbus Health: option 2 with a small tweak:
- Grant 1 month of dedicated throughput at their committed tier (no price change)
- Apply a 5% pro-rated invoice credit for October (instead of 6%) to avoid oversetting our current posture across similar incidents
- Make the offer contingent on a joint post-mortem within 7 business days and a follow-up validation run (we'll coordinate an on-call window)

If you agree, I approve moving forward; finance/legal will need to annotate the invoice and we should send a short customer comms doc (draft attached). Please capture the exec sign-off in HubSpot and route the DocuSign amendment link if they accept the month-of-dedicated-credit option.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success (acting)
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency + partial outage on 2026-10-31 — need exec approval for remedy

Marissa / Grace — I approve the recommendation as stated. A few operational notes:
- Finance: record a one-line invoice adjustment (5% credit) and a non-billable month for November (account-level adjustment) so customer's committed seat counts remain intact.
- Legal: no amendment required if the month-of-dedicated-credit is documented via an acceptance email and HubSpot activity; if Nimbus requests a contract change, escalate.
- Ops: schedule the joint post-mortem and set an on-call validation for Nov 5 (09:00–11:00 PT).

Grace, please send the customer comms (short, empathic, with clear next steps) and include the attachments we discussed. Once Nimbus signs off, finance will apply the credit. Marking as approved — you may proceed.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
